gaps.sentence: Stop ___ money on things you never use.
gaps.hint: to use money on useless things; -ing form after 'Stop'
gaps.explanation: waste money on something means to spend it on useless things; 'stop' is followed by the -ing form.

gaps.sentence: I'm ___ a course in web design this term.
gaps.explanation: do a course is the British English collocation for studying on a course.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: You should ___ track of your spending.
gaps.explanation: keep track of something means to stay informed about it.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.
